topic: Protected-contrast minimax simultaneous bands for a blind-replicate ADRF. Prove the matching expected-maximal-width statistical frontier using continuous integrated probability and signed marked-channel contrasts on a moment-derived protected frequency square, quantitative analytic continuation and Sobolev quotient recovery, measurable extrema over the theoretical exact compact continuous-channel profile, and a fixed-density, fixed-error Bernoulli marked converse. The band is an existence-level exact-profile procedure: no terminating finite cover or finitely checkable o(r_n) endpoint enclosure is proved, and effective finite-profile certification remains an explicit open computational question. This revives banked parent eid_blind_replicate_adrf_honest_supband_blind_cfzero_adrf_band with a different mathematical handle; the refuted empirical-grid/Jackson inverse and any oracle-dependent finite-witness construction are forbidden.

open_problems.open_problem: Can continuous integrated protected-cube probability and signed marked-channel contrasts yield a uniformly honest blind-replicate ADRF band with expected maximal width of order (log log n/log n)^(β-1/2)?

open_problems.why_unsolved: The banked parent establishes only qualitative contraction by compactness: its rejected empirical-grid/Jackson route put polynomial spatial-approximation error directly into forward tolerances even though analytic continuation amplifies that error nonlinearly, and grid feasibility does not control transforms between nodes. The web literature separately provides pointwise known-error ADRF inference and honest blind-replicate density inference, but not the paired causal numerator and design-density inverse or its sharp expected-width modulus. The missing first step is a nearly parametric continuous integrated contrast on a fixed protected cube for both the probability channel F_x and signed marked channel G_x, followed by quantitative continuation and stable recovery of q_x/f_x.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A quantitative inverse theorem for paired integrated probability and marked contrasts, followed by a measurable outer-profile band with uniform simultaneous coverage and matching upper and lower expected-width rate (log log n/log n)^(β-1/2).

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the closest causal estimand and measurement-error motivation while exposing the boundary of known-error, pointwise inference.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Scientific conclusions concern a continuous dose-response curve -> treatment is measured with error -> known-error deconvolution permits pointwise ADRF inference -> blind asymmetric replicates require an honest whole-curve width frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt protected-region integrated polynomial contrasts, nearly parametric forward control, analytic continuation, and Sobolev recovery simultaneously to F_x and signed G_x.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It treats the same blind two-replicate analytic inverse; the changed proof must handle a paired marked channel, a supremum target, and the causal quotient.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its self-normalized complex-moment test inversion and multiplier-bootstrap coverage proof after the protected inverse supplies a uniform linearization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its observation law and honest-band objective are adjacent, but its target is an unmarked latent density and it does not establish the requested width frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Propagate characteristic-function identities across isolated zeros using derivative information or exponential-tail analyticity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the identification bridge required before quantitative protected contrasts can recover both ADRF channels.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The parent obtained factorial attenuation for moment-annihilating marked perturbations but did not construct one packet simultaneously preserving Bernoulli means in [1/4,3/4], strict H^β slack, a fixed positive latent density, fixed asymmetric error laws, and a weighted chi-square or Hellinger bound for the convolved experiment. Published deconvolution packings perturb the latent density, so their hardness may reflect design uncertainty rather than ADRF uncertainty. The hard-family construction must instead freeze the entire unmarked replicate law, move only the bounded conditional outcome mark, and retain factorial attenuation after the blind convolution operator.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A fixed-nuisance two-point or finite-packing theorem giving valid Bernoulli potential outcomes, strict model-class membership, product-law total variation at most η<1-2α, and ADRF L∞ separation at least c(log log n/log n)^(β-1/2), implying the matching lower bound for every honest band.

writing_exemplar.why: Its ADRF formulation makes clear why causally valid lower alternatives must perturb conditional outcome means rather than merely a latent exposure density.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: The target is a continuous-treatment causal response -> replicate measurements reveal the latent dose only indirectly -> outcomes create a separate marked information channel -> sharp width requires indistinguishable models differing only in valid Bernoulli marks

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its compact-support moment-annihilating lower experiment and factorial transform attenuation while freezing the density and perturbing only a Bernoulli mark.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the same blind-replicate convolution geometry, but the resolution must replace L2 density separation by L∞ ADRF separation.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer its convolved bump-packing and divergence calculation after relocating each bump from the latent density to the conditional mark probability.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The inverse-channel lower-bound architecture is analogous even though the nuisance that is allowed to vary must change.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert indistinguishable separated curves into a finite-sample lower bound on confidence-band width rather than only point-estimation risk.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination criterion is expected maximal band width, so the marked packing needs a band-specific testing reduction.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the semi-infinite blind-replicate ADRF outer profile be replaced by a terminating certified finite optimization whose endpoint error is o((log log n/log n)^(β-1/2)) while controlling the continuous probability and marked-transform restrictions?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Finite-dimensional spline or atomic parameterization does not make the parent's continuum positivity, envelope, modulus, transform, and quotient restrictions decidable. Checking a mesh can either exclude the truth or miss violations and hence invalidate coverage; this is precisely why the forbidden empirical-grid/Jackson route cannot certify the profile. Neumann supplies a useful continuous probability topology and Kato–Sasaki–Ura supply implementable moment inversion, but neither proves a deterministic finite-to-continuum certificate for paired causal channels. The first changed step is to enclose every continuum constraint and objective with outward-rounded Bernstein, interval, or SOS bounds and propagate the deterministic optimization gap into the band endpoints.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A terminating algorithm returning rational outer endpoints and checkable certificates, together with a theorem proving containment of the exact continuous feasible profile, uniform simultaneous coverage, endpoint inflation o((log log n/log n)^(β-1/2)), and explicit complexity in n and the sieve dimensions.

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from fragile Kotlarski inversion to robust restriction inversion is the closest framing, with the destination changed to a continuous marked profile with a finite certificate.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Closed-form inversion is fragile -> valid complex moment restrictions survive -> sieve inversion yields an implementable confidence set -> continuous marked restrictions require certified finite profiling to preserve honesty

method_exemplars.technique: Use a continuum frequency-domain distance and integrated characteristic functions as measure-determining coordinates, then upgrade transform control to control of candidate probability laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the continuous-probability topology needed to replace an uncertified empirical grid.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert self-normalized complex moment tests over finite sieve coefficients with explicit approximation slack and multiplier-bootstrap critical values.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired finite outer profile is a continuum-certified, outcome-marked extension of this restriction-inversion program.

method_exemplars.technique: Couple suprema of growing empirical-process classes to Gaussian suprema using explicit entropy and envelope bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After deterministic certification of the continuum, this machinery can deliver simultaneous critical values for paired marked and unmarked contrasts.

source_refs.claim: Gives sufficient and, in some settings, necessary conditions under which characteristic-function zeros do not reduce density-deconvolution accuracy.
source_refs.author: Denis Belomestny and Alexander Goldenshluger

source_refs.claim: Shows zeros and oscillations can be rate-neutral for several replicated-measurement functionals, without treating a marked causal ratio or band width.

source_refs.claim: Shows identification may survive isolated or arbitrary zeros through derivative identities and analytic continuation under tail restrictions.
source_refs.author: Kirill Evdokimov and Halbert White

open_problems.why_unsolved: The parent fixes a moment envelope and hence a protected cube, while adjacent spectral-band work assumes a fixed positive separation. Published results show that zeros can be harmless for unmarked density or distribution recovery and that identification can cross zero sets analytically, but an ADRF is a two-channel quotient: protection or cancellation in the probability transform need not persist in the marked transform. Under triangular arrays, shrinking ν_n, c_n, or increasing zero multiplicity affect contrast estimation, continuation, and denominator stability on different scales. The fixed-cube polynomial contrast must therefore be recalibrated on a shrinking protected region and matched to local marked alternatives with the same deteriorating geometry.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Matching upper and lower theorems for an explicit rate R_n(c_n,ν_n,β,κ) indexed by zero multiplicity or tail geometry, including rate-neutral, logarithmically costly, nonshrinking, and nonidentifiable regimes plus a coverage-valid band across their boundaries.

writing_exemplar.why: Its ADRF formulation exposes division by the treatment-error transform as the boundary whose deterioration must be converted into a causal width phase diagram.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: ADRF localization becomes deconvolution under dose error -> inversion depends on channel strength and zero geometry -> blind replicates make that strength unknown -> characterize exactly when an honest causal band can still shrink

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its zero-bearing deconvolution construction and matched necessity arguments while tracking two protected channels rather than one density transform.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its zero-neutrality frontier is the nearest template for the requested ADRF phase diagram.

method_exemplars.technique: Track continuation across zero sets through derivative identities and exponential-tail analyticity with constants explicit in ν_n and zero multiplicity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired phase boundaries depend on the quantitative stability of precisely this identification step.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt weak-, semi-strong-, and strong-identification asymptotics and boundary-valid critical-value arguments to drifting transform strength.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A channel-strength phase diagram likewise requires inference that remains valid across changing identification regimes.

open_problems.open_problem: Is there an observable cross-channel self-similarity condition under which one blind-replicate ADRF band adapts honestly to unknown β and unknown channel severity, while honest adaptation is impossible over the unrestricted union of paired Sobolev classes?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Adaptive estimation does not provide the bias certificate required for honest bands. Ordinary self-similarity cannot simply be imposed separately on f_x and q_x because cancellation in q_x/f_x may make the ADRF smoother than either channel, while blind convolution can hide shell energy differently in probability and marked contrasts. Unknown zero or tail severity adds a second adaptation axis, so known-operator wavelet selection does not control under-smoothing uniformly. The first missing step is an observable paired contrast-separation condition that consistently certifies continuation bias and operator severity for a data-driven cutoff.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient theorem defining an observable paired self-similar subclass, constructing one uniformly honest band attaining each oracle width rate across a stated range of β and channel-severity classes, and proving a testing lower bound against adaptation over the unrestricted union.

writing_exemplar.why: It gives the canonical framing that separates adaptive estimation from honest adaptive bands and motivates self-similarity as the missing restriction.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Smoothness is unknown -> adaptive estimators are available -> honest adaptive bands fail on unrestricted classes -> identify the paired observable condition restoring adaptation for a blind ADRF

method_exemplars.technique: Use multiscale self-similarity to bound bias from observable coefficients and pair an adaptive construction with an indistinguishability-based necessity proof.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested theorem has the same construction-and-impossibility form, but its observable coefficients are protected paired contrasts.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt operator-calibrated wavelet thresholding and its sup-norm oracle proof to an estimated, zero-bearing replicate channel.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the multiscale inverse-problem selector whose bias control must be made cross-channel and blind.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine Gaussian anti-concentration, multiplier bootstrap, and bootstrap Lepski selection to preserve coverage after data-driven resolution choice.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the closest simultaneous-inference machinery for converting a resolution selector into an honest adaptive band.

literature_map:
Huang and Zhang (2023, JRSSB, arXiv:2211.04642) are the direct ADRF anchor: known-error deconvolution and pointwise asymptotic inference.
Kennedy, Ma, McHugh, and Small (2017, JRSSB, arXiv:1507.00747) provide the error-free doubly robust dose-response mapping and flag uniform band inference as future work.
Colangelo and Lee (2025, JBES, arXiv:2004.03036) provide kernel-localized DML and uniform inference for correctly measured continuous treatments.
Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:0804.0713) show that replicates can recover known-error first-order performance under smoother repeated-error regimes.
Neumann (2007, JMVA, DOI 10.1016/j.jmva.2006.09.012) uses continuous integrated characteristic functions for blind-panel consistency under weak zero-set conditions.
Evdokimov and White (2012, Econometric Theory, DOI 10.1017/S0266466611000831) cross isolated or arbitrary zeros through derivative identities and analytic continuation.
Meister and Neumann (2010, Statistica Sinica 20:1609–1636) show zeros can be rate-neutral for replicated-measurement density, distribution, and support estimation.
Belomestny and Goldenshluger (2021, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1907.11024) establish optimal zero-bearing deconvolution and zero-neutrality conditions.
Kato and Sasaki (2018, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1608.02251) construct multiplier-bootstrap density bands using auxiliary error information.
Kato and Sasaki (2019, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1702.03377) construct uniform EIV-regression bands under validation or auxiliary-error structures.
Kato, Sasaki, and Ura (2021, Quantitative Economics, arXiv:1808.09375) invert complex repeated-measurement moment restrictions but target density and leave sharp rates unresolved.
Kurisu and Otsu (2022, JMVA, DOI 10.1016/j.jmva.2021.104921) obtain subsampling bands for repeated-measurement density and distribution estimators, not causal marked contrasts.
Lounici and Nickl (2011, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1103.1489) provide the closest sup-norm deconvolution upper/lower architecture.
Genovese and Wasserman (2008, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:math/0701513) and Bull (2012, EJS, arXiv:1110.4985) supply band-width and honest-adaptation lower-bound machinery.
The unoccupied intersection is a causal ADRF band using fully blind zero-bearing replicates, continuous protected marked contrasts, certified finite profiling, and a matching fixed-density Bernoulli-marked width converse.
